record.paper_title: Some open problems in dynamical systems
record.original_question: For n ≥ 3, can one find a smooth Hamiltonian H in a sufficiently small C^k neighborhood (with k ≥ 2) of the integrable Hamiltonian H_0(r) = ½\|r\|^2 on T^*T^n such that the Hamiltonian flow of H on the energy hypersurface H^{-1}(1) has at least one dense orbit?

evidence.quote: 6.2 - Questions. 1. Can one ﬁnd an example of a C∞ -Hamiltonian H in a small Ck-neighbourhoodk≥ 2 of H0(r) = 1/2∥r∥2 such that, on H−1(1), the Hamiltonian ﬂow of H has one dense orbit ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 3$ and consider the cotangent bundle $T^*\mathbb{T}^n \cong \mathbb{T}^n \times \mathbb{R}^n$ with canonical coordinates $(\theta, r)$ and the standard symplectic form $\sum_i d\theta_i \wedge dr_i$. Define the integrable Hamiltonian
$$H_0(\theta, r) = \tfrac{1}{2}\|r\|^2.$$
Fix an integer $k \geq 2$. Question: does there exist a smooth ($C^\infty$) Hamiltonian $H$ on $T^*\mathbb{T}^n$ lying in an arbitrarily small $C^k$-neighborhood of $H_0$ such that the Hamiltonian flow of $H$, restricted to the energy hypersurface $H^{-1}(1)$, possesses at least one dense orbit?
artifact.status_search_result: The question (often attributed to Herman, 1998 ICM) appears to remain open. Partial progress was obtained by Kaloshin and Saprykina (Comm. Math. Phys. 2012), who constructed a nearly integrable Hamiltonian with an orbit dense in a set of maximal Hausdorff dimension on the unit energy surface, but not dense in the full energy surface. The full quasi-ergodic-type question with a single orbit dense in $H^{-1}(1)$ has not, to current knowledge, been resolved.

status_evidence.title: An Example of a Nearly Integrable Hamiltonian System with a Trajectory Dense in a Set of Maximal Hausdorff Dimension
status_evidence.snippet: Kaloshin–Saprykina construct H_0+εH_1 with an orbit dense in a set of maximal Hausdorff dimension on the unit energy surface near H_0(I)=|I|^2/2.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress: a dense orbit on a subset of full Hausdorff dimension, not the entire energy surface.

status_evidence.title: Fayad – Topological mixing and quasi-ergodicity
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Herman's question and the state of the art on dense/quasi-ergodic orbits near integrable Hamiltonians.
status_evidence.claim: Herman's dense-orbit question is referenced as still being investigated.
